purpose: Keep model spend proportional to the evidence obligation. Use the least expensive model tier that can satisfy the task, escalate only when capability or consequence justifies it, and make expensive reruns granular rather than habitual.
principle: Capability is a budgeted resource, not a default setting.
rules: Estimate or bound the cost of a multi-call workflow before execution when provider pricing and expected token volume are knowable.
Prefer a balanced or economical model for routine routing, extraction, classification, formatting, and already-bounded work.
Escalate to a frontier model only when the cheaper tier fails, the task has a materially higher consequence boundary, or the benchmark explicitly requires frontier behavior.
Record why a frontier escalation was necessary when the workflow emits a receipt.

Do not rerun model slots that already produced valid evidence when an unrelated provider, parser, or harness component failed; rerun only the affected slot whenever the execution environment permits it.
Reuse deterministic outputs and previously verified artifacts when their inputs and authority have not changed.
Keep cost ceilings cross-provider rather than allowing each provider to spend independently without a total workflow budget.
Fail closed or require explicit authorization when projected spend exceeds a configured workflow ceiling.
Never trade away accounting, provenance, authority, or safety invariants merely to reduce token cost.

routing.principle: Route by seat, express the seat as a capability tier, and treat the concrete model ID as today's perishable answer.

layers.seat: the job in the workflow, such as lead loop, code or audit worker, design or copy worker; durable
layers.tier: the capability class that seat needs, such as fast, reasoning, frontier; durable
layers.model_id: the concrete model serving that tier today; perishable

rules: Write every reference outside the pin in tier or family-relative form. A sentence that becomes false when a provider ships a new version number is written in the wrong form.
Pin concrete model IDs in exactly one place per deployment, with the date they were verified. A second copy of the pin is a second place to go stale.
Refresh the pin from a live authority such as the provider's model listing, never from memory. Never construct or guess a model ID; a plausible-looking ID is not a real one.
When a model family is renamed, retired, or added, re-pin the tier and leave the seat routing unchanged.
Spend a premium tier on purpose for named seats, not by default for whole categories of work.

benchmark_exception.rule: A benchmark may intentionally exercise frontier and balanced tiers to measure capability differences. Benchmark breadth does not justify wasteful reruns: isolate model slots and preserve valid receipts whenever possible.

recommended_runtime_controls.default_numeric_values: unset; host or operator chooses based on provider pricing and use case

promotion_rule: Do not add a canonical Dale OS skill for model-cost optimization until recurring evidence demonstrates a distinct failure class with its own trigger, boundary, falsifier, and eval corpus.
